THE WORK BETWEEN THE BYTES

Small enough to understand.

01 / NETWORK

Asynchronous sessions

Beast handles HTTP framing. Asio moves the bytes. Each connection keeps its own parser, buffer, and ordered response stream.

02 / CONTENT

Your routes. Your files.

Define fixed responses in JSON and serve files from a chosen document root, with bounded caching and metadata checks.

Limits you can read

Connection caps, request-size limits, and socket deadlines are part of the runtime. The implementation and tests are in the open.

R. AMOGH / SYSTEMS PROJECT

Understand the
work behind a request.

I built Tez to work through the details of an HTTP server in C++: ownership, parsing, connection lifetimes, file access, and the tradeoffs between them.

The current direction

Tez uses Boost.Beast for HTTP/1.x parsing and Boost.Asio for asynchronous socket I/O. Configured routes are loaded once. Static file access stays behind an explicit document root.

The goal is a codebase whose behavior is visible and testable. Socket tests exercise framing and connection behavior; component tests check routing, file access, and cache rules.

The boundaries

This is a development project, with no current throughput ranking or production-readiness guarantee. Filesystem reads and logging are synchronous inside I/O handlers.

TLS, authentication, per-client rate limiting, HTTP/2, and durable application storage are not implemented. The API endpoints demonstrate dispatch; they do not store resources.

READ. BUILD. QUESTION.

The source is the starting point.

Build instructions, design notes, tests, and contribution guidelines live in the repository.
